items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw5y: Vučić, Serbia's leader for 12 years, conceded defeat in snap elections to a student-led protest movement, saying "it is clear that we have lost." Record turnout favored the movement, which grew from two years of protests after a train-station canopy collapse in Novi Sad killed 16, seen as a symbol of corruption. Celebrations erupted after his concession.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2: Lula defeated far-right Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil's presidential run-off, winning just over 51% to Bolsonaro's 48% after more than 64 million votes, a historic comeback since he lost the first round. His Workers' Party called it "a historic turning point for democracy," though the process was marred by allegations of voter suppression in public transport.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Switzerland says Nigeria's first Ebola patient in over a decade, a Swiss diplomat's Ugandan-born wife, likely caught the virus while traveling in Uganda, not Congo as Uganda had claimed. The outbreak, first detected in DR Congo in May, has now reached Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria, making it the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history and raising containment concerns.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckpd: Israel heads into a tightly contested general election on Tuesday after three years of regional war, with polls showing the governing coalition and opposition near tied. Half a million first-time voters and about 70,000 Israelis flying in from abroad are expected to vote. Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a new opposition face challenging PM Netanyahu.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: With US midterms just over a week away, Trump launched another fierce anti-Muslim attack on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. El-Sayed is running against Republican Mike Rogers, a race seen as potentially pivotal to which party controls the US Senate.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o: Lewis Hamilton, 41, hopes to keep racing into the early 2030s so he can compete in F1's new African Grand Prix, confirmed for Rwanda on a purpose-built circuit near Kigali under a 10-year deal. It marks F1's return to Africa for the first time since 1993, despite criticism of Rwanda's human rights record.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq8e: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home after more than 10 months in exile, greeted by crowds of supporters as she traveled toward Caracas. She left in January, a month before the US seized President Nicolás Maduro and backed his deputy Delcy Rodríguez as interim leader, who later signed an oil deal granting the US favorable terms.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10: Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, 19, is campaigning to become the youngest-ever Ballon d'Or winner, aiming to beat Ronaldo Nazário's record of winning at 21. The teenager won the 2026 World Cup with Spain just after turning 19 and lifted the La Liga title with Barcelona, though an injury-hit season complicates his bid.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: A US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns in Guinea-Bissau, funded by the CDC and Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Foundation, has been halted after failing to get government approval, the lead researcher said. The $3.2m study drew global backlash as unethical; critics like vaccine expert Paul Offit argued the money should simply fund vaccination instead of research.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvx2: Elon Musk said SpaceX had restricted Ukraine's Starlink service, accusing Kyiv of violating terms of service by using it for military drone strikes, before service was restored. The row followed a wider US-Ukraine dispute over strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, and came after Trump said he'd told Musk to "put it back," despite earlier denying involvement.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/h: Historian Romila Thapar, 96, said colonial historians reshaped how Indian history is understood by reducing complex social and political processes to simplified religious narratives, laying groundwork for today's Hindutva reading of history. Speaking at a memorial lecture for CPI(M) leader Sitaram Yechury, she said history "is playing a public role" it never did before.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/with-an-: Rajkumar Rajbhar, on trial for a 2016 murder, tried to escape it by faking his own death, submitting a death certificate with photos showing him on a funeral pyre - using a goat in his place.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: An under-construction house collapsed in northeast Delhi's Harsh Vihar on Sunday evening, trapping at least two people - reportedly the contractor and his father - under debris. Fire tenders and NDRF teams launched a rescue operation; the ground floor was an older structure with new construction underway on the first floor.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/c: A depression over the Bay of Bengal is set to intensify into a "very severe cyclonic storm," per the IMD, with winds of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph, and cross the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast by October 28. It's expected to be more intense than last year's Montha cyclone; Odisha has activated disaster response with a zero-casualty goal.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/kerala-j: A Kerala judge's minor son rammed a Mercedes-Benz into a scooter rider, who died. The judge, posted in Thrissur and the car's registered owner, is being examined for liability and may be named an accused.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Former Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud rejected ex-judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul's memoir account of judicial appointments, saying collegium decisions were unanimous and Kaul endorsed every recommendation without ever dissenting. Chandrachud said he hadn't yet read Kaul's upcoming memoir "Without Fear or Favour" but noted the collegium's resolutions and reasoning are public on the Supreme Court's website.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/r: MNS chief Raj Thackeray deleted a social media post sharing a documentary on PM Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani, at the request of Mumbai's Police Commissioner, but vowed to keep opposing "corporate monopolies." The video, shared by Sabeer Bhatia, had gained 4.8 million views on X, and Thackeray said it had already achieved its purpose.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/15-shops: A fire destroyed 15 shops and a hotel in a Jammu market, with losses estimated in crores. Fire and emergency services rushed to the scene, but the blaze spread rapidly, burning through shops within minutes.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: India's Enforcement Directorate arrested six people and froze 1,424 bank accounts in Manipur and Mizoram, busting a cross-border "narco-hawala" network that moves drug proceeds from across India back to suppliers in Myanmar. The Northeast's porous 1,643km border with Myanmar has become a major corridor for heroin and methamphetamine entering India and Bangladesh.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Apple's India software unit, Apple Operations India, reported ₹650 crore in software and global-support revenue for FY26, pushing total revenue past ₹1,400 crore - a sharp rise from last year. Manufacturing-support revenue nearly doubled too, signaling Apple is building out its Indian subsidiary into a major global engineering hub.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Senco Gold agreed to buy a 68% stake in August Jewellery, which runs the digital-first "Melorra" jewellery brand, for ₹68 crore, in tranches through February 2027. Including a promoter-group purchase, Senco's total stake will reach 79%, making August Jewellery a subsidiary - a move aimed at strengthening Senco's digital and omnichannel reach to younger buyers.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Fairfax-controlled IIFL Capital hired four senior private bankers from Barclays - Neeraj Pandey, Subir Didwania, Kunal Kapadia and Vivek Makim - to expand its wealth management business targeting ultra-high-net-worth families and non-resident Indians. The hires, with decades of combined private-banking experience, come as global banks restructure and competition for wealthy Indian clients intensifies.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's largest companies are preparing for Ind AS 118, a new accounting standard that changes how income, expenses and operating profit must be classified and reported. The shift brings complex new requirements and system changes, and audit committees are drawing up transition plans while awaiting final regulatory guidance.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Capital is moving from India's secondary stock market into a roughly ₹5 trillion pipeline of IPOs and share placements, says fund manager Madhu Lunawat. Retail investors, worried about 10-12% personal inflation, are chasing small- and mid-cap stocks, while foreign investors stay cautious due to high valuations, a weaker rupee and scarce high-growth, reasonably priced companies.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck87: UK Chancellor John Healey is keeping unusually tight secrecy around his upcoming Budget, splitting details into "compartments" and using codenames to prevent leaks that destabilized markets before the last Budget. Growth has beaten expectations and the IMF has praised the UK for planning to cut borrowing, but the piece warns tougher conditions may emerge from January.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: JSW Steel says it is managing geopolitical uncertainty well while investing heavily in capacity as India's steel demand stays strong, aided by an improved IMF growth outlook. The company reported an inventory drawdown signaling solid demand, and says internal accruals and debt reduction have put it in a strong position to expand and focus on high-value products.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: India's consumer regulator CCPA fined Hogar Technologies ₹1 lakh for misleading walkie-talkie advertisements that failed to disclose operating frequencies, licensing requirements and other regulatory information needed for informed buying decisions.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: JSW Group, while seeking to raise its stake in JSW MG Motor India, remains heavily reliant on Chinese partner SAIC Motor, which supplied about 70% of the joint venture's FY26 purchases - roughly $840 million including royalties and license fees, up from $640 million in FY25. The figures highlight the carmaker's continued dependence on Chinese supply chains.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's Competition Commission (CCI) plans to hire 41 people across departments, including its investigation arm, the office of the director general, according to public recruitment notices.
items.https://inc42.com/features/growth-vs-pro: Swiggy's shares fell about 15% to ₹179.90, erasing roughly ₹9,000 crore in market value, after Q2 FY27 results showed Instamart's widening losses overshadowing improving food-delivery profits. Revenue rose 36.1% year-on-year to ₹7,571 crore and net loss narrowed to ₹922 crore from a year earlier, though it widened versus the prior quarter.
items.https://entrackr.com/report/weekly-fundi: Indian startups raised $133.9 million this week across 15 deals, down sharply from $302.85 million the previous week. Growth-stage deals led with $86.2 million, including Even Healthcare's $50 million Series B from Khosla Ventures; early-stage startups raised $47.7 million, led by AI firm AuxoAI's $20.7 million round from NTTVC.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Honasa Consumer has promoted Vipul Maheshwari to chief product & technology officer, overseeing product, technology, engineering and analytics. He will lead the company's push into AI, including agentic AI that can carry out multi-step tasks with human oversight.
items.https://inc42.com/features/flipkarts-sum: Flipkart has seen 14 senior-level exits in the past year, with three more VPs - including product and smartphones leaders - set to leave, as the e-commerce giant faces uncertainty over a possible IPO and employee stock liquidity. Walmart is pushing for profitability even as Flipkart keeps investing heavily in quick commerce and food delivery.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/unicommer: E-commerce SaaS firm Unicommerce grew Q2 FY27 revenue 15% year-on-year to ₹59.10 crore and net profit 10.7% to ₹6.4 crore, per unaudited results. First-half FY27 revenue rose 14.7% to ₹110.45 crore, though expenses grew faster - employee costs up 23.4% and server hosting costs up 41.5% - as the company keeps scaling.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Tender247, an AI-powered platform that helps businesses track government tender opportunities, has appointed actor Anupam Kher as its brand ambassador as it works to simplify the tender process for smaller businesses.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma scored centuries to help India beat Zimbabwe by 121 runs and seal the ODI series. Vaishnavi Sharma, playing only her second ODI, took four wickets in the win.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Manchester United fans sang support for manager Michael Carrick during a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth, even as they voiced anger at almost everything else at the club. With eight games without a win - United's worst run since 2015-16 - and two bad losses in a week, Carrick's job is now in serious doubt.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/h: India beat Zimbabwe by 121 runs in the second ODI to seal an unassailable 2-0 series lead, as Deepti Sharma smashed a century while Harmanpreet Kaur played a steadier supporting innings in a record 153-run fifth-wicket stand. India had slipped to 19 for two early on before the partnership, following Pratika Rawal's earlier century, turned the match around.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: ESPNcricinfo looks at who stays and who goes for Australia's cricket team, with Green's return raising fresh selection questions ahead of a key debate over the squad's make-up.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/art: Kimi Antonelli, 20, dominated the United States Grand Prix but still must wait to clinch his first F1 title, leading Mercedes teammate George Russell by 123 points with Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc behind. He'll be crowned champion next weekend in Mexico City unless he loses more than 23 points to Russell or 24 to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/denso-iri: Japan's Denso Iris beat China's Sichuan Yuanda Meile 81-63 in the FIBA Women's Basketball League Asia final, relying on collective team play rather than foreign imports. Sichuan struggled after star American Chennedy Carter was disqualified early in the second quarter for two technical fouls, and Iris extended its lead steadily through each quarter.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/25/grok-r: Grok has released just the first seven minutes of its promised full-length AI-generated "Odyssey" movie, three months after Elon Musk said it would be a complete, "historically accurate" film - now calling it merely "Episode 1." Musk had criticized director Christopher Nolan's own big-budget, practically-filmed version of the same story for its casting choices.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: As enterprise AI matures, the competitive edge is shifting from which model a company uses to the "serving harness" built around it - the architecture, memory management and scheduling that determine whether AI can run reliably and economically at scale. There is no universally best model, the piece argues, only the right engineering fit for each specific business problem.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/25/ai-del: Apollo Global Management's chief economist Torsten Slok says AI has delivered "zero financial payoff" to corporate America outside the tech industry, based on flat profit margins and revenue per worker across the S&P 500 excluding the seven biggest tech giants. He argues AI functions mainly as "a great calculator" so far, with no clear sign it is lifting broader corporate productivity.
items.https://www.theverge.com/column/1017983/: Google's shift to AI-driven search, including AI Overviews launched in 2024 that summarize web content directly in results, has upended the online publishing industry that long relied on search traffic. Publishers who spent years optimizing pages to rank on Google are now finding it harder to survive, as the AI summaries reduce the clicks search once reliably sent their way.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/25/the-ho: TechCrunch rounds up popular AI wearables like Muse Charm, Bee, Friend and Plaud that aim to weave AI into daily life as productivity tools or companions. Amazon-owned Bee, a $49.99 pendant that records surroundings to create reminders and notes, has spawned newer devices like the $74.99 Bee Frontier; even OpenAI is reportedly building its own compact AI companion gadget.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: BBC's upcoming nature series Blue Planet III is deliberately keeping imperfect shots - stray plankton, a boat or buoy in frame - that earlier versions would have cut, to prove its footage is genuinely real rather than AI-generated. Producer Elizabeth White said overly polished, seamless footage is now "a dead giveaway" of AI, so the show embraces a rougher, more organic look.
items.https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10: Hackers exploited critical flaws in a widely used programming language for four days before public disclosure, Amazon said; the bugs, found with AI assistance, are now being "broadly exploited" worldwide after going undetected for over a decade. The US NSA and UK authorities warned websites were critically exposed, and some European governments took sites offline to patch them.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: Enterprise AI can speed up decisions and automate tasks, but without understanding how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss key constraints, says Celonis chief scientist Devavrat Shah. He argues effective "decision intelligence" requires connecting AI to a company's real workflows and data so agents grasp context, rather than working in a vacuum where they risk costly mistakes.

Beyond GPU costs, AI's expenses include a large, often-overlooked data storage bill, since every inference request - unlike one-off model training - leaves data behind indefinitely. Storage firm WD found that an 8-second AI-generated video clip delivered as a 3.97MB file actually left over 500MB of associated back-end data, showing inference costs keep accumulating long after a model responds.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Moderators of the Reddit community r/opensource introduced new submission rules banning projects that use AI, among other restrictions on the subreddit.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/10/: Google has quietly updated its privacy policy, removing language that explicitly promised not to use Gmail, Drive or Photos content for ad personalization. The change opens the door to using that data for ads once it's shared with other Google services via its "Personal Intelligence" feature, launched in early 2026, which lets users pool data across apps for Google's AI products.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/intel: The US FCC's ban on foreign-made robots created confusion for chipmaker Intel, which relies on foreign-built automated guided vehicles to move materials in its US chip fabs. The FCC granted Intel a one-year waiver on October 22 "out of an abundance of caution," letting it keep using robots - often made by Japanese firms like Murata Machinery and Daifuku - while it adjusts.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: A scalable enterprise AI system needs data, engineering, platforms, operating models and governance to work together, according to this MIT Technology Review EmTech Future session. Vanguard's Jing Wang, who leads its Center for AI & Insights and previously worked at Boston Consulting Group, discusses building that foundation in a regulated environment to turn AI into lasting value for investors.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed a law requiring labels on ads - video, audio, images or text - that are "significantly modified or generated" by AI, applying to everything from TV commercials to small restaurant flyers. It's among the first such state laws, but has loopholes: exemptions for parody, satire and "evidently fictional" content leave key terms subjective and unclear.
